In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a cell type and a gene that can be used in a cell therapy approach to SCI.
the development of a cell-based therapy for SCI.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for SCI, and may contribute to the development of new cell-based strategies for SCI treatment in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
grafting hENPs transgenic for Ngn2 is a promising approach for functional recovery after SCI, and that naïve hENP grafting is not beneficial.
the use of Ngn2-transduced hENPs, but not naïve hENP grafting, is beneficial in a rat model of SCI.
transplantation of Ngn2 expressing hENPs improves functional recovery after severe spinal injury, and that naïve-hENP grafting is not beneficial in this model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of Ngn2 expressing hENPs may represent a promising approach for the treatment of spinal cord injury.
transplantation of hNPs transduced with Ngn2 is able to promote axonal sprouting and improve motor recovery after severe SCI.
transplantation of hNgn2-hENPs is beneficial for motor recovery after SCI, and this effect is independent from the graft survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type of cells used in SCI should be carefully chosen, and that the use of naïve cells should be avoided in favor of cells expressing specific factors able to stimulate axonal growth.
the choice of the right cell population is of primary importance for successful cell therapy in SCI.
Ngn2 expression in hENPs is a promising approach to improve functional recovery after severe SCI.
